Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Brazil’s presidential run-off debate turned personal days before voting, intensifying a tight race between the incumbent left and right-wing challenger.
• Alberta votes on whether to hold a referendum on independence from Canada; polls suggest a preference to remain but the debate is divisive.
• Ukraine accuses the U.S. of restricting access to Starshield satellite communications, as transatlantic coordination strains under wartime pressures.
• Emmanuel Macron rejected his interior minister’s resignation amid riots, underscoring France’s political strains and market jitters.
• Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu and separately drew Republican ire over a Russia sanctions waiver, while the UK rebuked comments downplaying NATO allies’ role in Afghanistan.
Why it matters: Democratic tests, alliance tensions and domestic unrest across multiple regions are reshaping diplomatic alignments and political risk.

• Italy detained more than 200 people during two days of rioting; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called an emergency meeting.
• The World Food Programme cut aid to 500,000 people in Gaza amid funding shortfalls, warning fragile gains in food security could reverse.
• Israeli police arrested 10 people after settler attacks on a journalist and diplomats; the U.S. ambassador called it a “despicable act of terror.”
• In Kenya, a pastor accused of ordering parents to starve their children faces a verdict in a case involving 191 murder charges.
Why it matters: Social unrest and humanitarian pressures are testing governments’ legitimacy and capacity to protect rights and public safety.

Society & Human Rights.title: First Thing: US ambassador in rare diplomatic break with Israel over attack on US journalist
Society & Human Rights.text: Mike Huckabee condemns attack on Washington Post photojournalist that has drawn lukewarm response from Israeli authorities. Plus, Japan is attempting to boldly go where no space mission has gone beforeDon’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up hereGood morning. The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced a settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror”.Levine, 63, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinians attempting to harvest their olives. The photographer, who is in hospital recovering from hand surgery, broken ribs and other injuries, said she was beaten for more than 10 minutes.What else has Heidi Levine said about the attack? She said: “I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily, I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking and kicking me. I’ve been covering this region for over 40 years and I have never seen this country in such a state as it is today. I’ve invested decades of blood, sweat and tears into this. They cracked my bones, they haven’t cracked my spirit.”How have Israeli authorities responded? In a move Levine said left her “shocked and insulted”, Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has been ambiguous in addressing the assault. He said he condemned “violence against anyone” but referred to the attack as “alleged” and said its circumstances remained unclear.What is causing the wave of protests across Europe? School conditions, housing costs and the cost of living have brought demonstrators on to the streets in several countries including Spain, France and Portugal. Protests in Albania against the prime minister, Edi Rama, entered their sixth day on Sunday. Demonstrators there have said they are unhappy with perceived corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. Continue reading...

Entertainment.title: Getting Ready for the Night Shift Is Like Clockwork for Naz Hassan
Entertainment.text: If there’s one process that signals the start of chef Naz Hassan’s night, it’s changing his shoes. Having worked in kitchens across Milan and now London, the simple act of swapping his lace-ups for a pair of work-ready clogs remains constant, helping him get physically and mentally into gear for a busy shift making Italian plates.Exploring what functionality in style means to the chef, Hypebeast heads to his acclaimed neighborhood restaurant, Ornella, for a new two-part UGG campaign. With the debut installment capturing stylist Joel Lyall moving through the night, the latest feature shows how Hassan adapts to the energy behind the counter, as well as the moment he winds down with the brand’s functional Fall 2026 offering. "During a busy day, we’re like an orchestra, and everyone needs to play their instrument in the best way."“Service starts when the first customer comes through the door,” Hassan explains, once he’s slipped into his chef whites and the UGG Otzo Western Clog. “What kicks in is that sense of duty: you have to perform because you’re selling goods that need to be served to the highest level it possibly can.” Today, the chef begins service by making risotto, one of his favorite dishes on the menu. “During a busy day, we’re like an orchestra, and everyone needs to play their instrument in the best way,” he shares. It's not just about the individual performance, though. Hassan mentions how, more importantly, they need to “stay in harmony” so the kitchen can run like clockwork. To keep him in top form, he is drawn to the silhouette’s contoured EVA footbed and lightweight rubber outsole for its support throughout the day. “Having a comfortable pair of shoes is non-negotiable because I’m standing on my feet for 16 hours,” he says. “Shoes are the only part of my uniform that can be personalized, so it's nice when I can bring a bit of myself to my work.”Though Hassan has over a decade of experience perfecting his routine to meet the demands of restaurants, his success comes down to the customers. “What has kept me going when I work at night is seeing the smiles when people enjoy my food,” he reflects on his time as a chef. “The best memories I have are around the table at Christmas, Diwali and birthday parties, so I want them just to enjoy the moment and forget they’re in a restaurant.”"Having a comfortable pair of shoes is non-negotiable because I’m standing on my feet for 16 hours."Hassan clocks out of his shift by switching his clogs for the more weather-appropriate UGG Loften Chukka for his journey home. A lace-up leather shoe with a hard-wearing base and cozy sheepskin-lined tongue, the chef shares how it helps him adapt to temperature changes, saying, “To be able to step out of the hot kitchen with this warm feeling on your feet on a very cold night is perfect.” After resting up after a long night, he adopts a slower pace the next morning. Maintaining an element of calm, he walks around his local area and picks up coffee and pastry before preparing for yet another day of service at his restaurants. Entertainment.title: Quentin Tarantino Confirms Finishing Script for 10th Film but Delays Production to "Live a Little"
Entertainment.text: SummaryQuentin Tarantino has completed writing the script for his tenth and final feature filmThe filmmaker is delaying production to focus on his London stage play 'The Popinjay Cavalier' and spend time with familyThe swashbuckling comedy starring Sacha Baron Cohen opens at the Phoenix Theatre next March and runs through June 13Quentin Tarantino has completed the script for his 10th feature film, though the director plans to hold off on production until his London stage production finishes its run. The filmmaker shared the update during an appearance on The Graham Norton Show, marking his first visit to the program in over a decade.Tarantino reaffirmed his longstanding plan to retire from filmmaking after ten features, but made it clear that he will not rush into production. "I've written a script that I really like, but I want to do the play and see who I am; then I'll then go back and spend time with my family and live a little and then see what I want to do,” Tarantino said.His immediate creative focus is centered on The Popinjay Cavalier, which originated as a screenplay before transitioning into a stage production. “It really worked as a play,” Tarantino explained, adding, “I think it will be thrilling.” Billed as a swashbuckling comedy starring Sacha Baron Cohen, the production marks the filmmaker’s West End debut following his 2019 Oscar-winning film Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. “I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino noted.The Popinjay Cavalier begins previews in late February before officially opening at London’s Phoenix Theatre next March, running through June 13.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

The appearance marked the KHY founder’s first time ever walking a Victoria’s Secret catwalk.Designed by Jacob Arabo, the showpiece drew inspiration from Jacob & Co.’s Rare Touch Jewelry Collection and reimagined the traditional lingerie staple without using any fabric. Handcrafted by 15 artisans over more than 1,000 hours, the structure incorporates 3,218 individually designed components engineered to move with the body like lingerie. At the center sits a 75.54-carat natural Fancy Vivid Yellow diamond, encircled by 4,409 natural diamonds totaling 1,373 carats in an array of cuts, including the jeweler's signature Angel-Cut. Made entirely of precious metals and stones, covered in shimmering crystals, and finished with delicate fringe along the base, the $50 million USD piece stands as the most valuable Fantasy Bra ever produced.Jenner paired the diamond-encrusted top with a low-slung silver thong, an iridescent white miniskirt, clear PVC heels, and large feathery white wings as partner Timothée Chalamet and mother Kris Jenner cheered from the audience. The runway appearance brought the Fantasy Bra back to the stage for the first time since Elsa Hosk wore it in 2018, following historic iterations previously donned by Claudia Schiffer in 1996, Alessandra Ambrosio, and Adriana Lima. Longevity & Anti-Aging.title: Predicting Inflammation and Disease Risk with Gut Microbiome Composition
Longevity & Anti-Aging.text: The gut microbiome changes with age, and evidence suggests that this provides a meaningful contribution to degeneration and disease. Microbial populations that provoke chronic inflammation grow in size at the expense of populations that produce beneficial metabolites. Researchers here show that gut microbiome composition is a better predictor of the burden of inflammation and risk of disease than chronological age, much as one might expect given what is known of age-related changes in gut microbiome composition, and also given that researchers have built aging clocks from gut microbiome data. It is one more argument for a greater focus on the development and availability of therapeutic approaches capable of lasting rejuvenation of the gut microbiome, such as fecal microbiota transplantation and flagellin immunization. Longevity & Anti-Aging.title: Insights from the Genome of the Aldabra Giant Tortoise
Longevity & Anti-Aging.text: The oldest land animal with an established age is an Aldabra giant tortoise, at 194 years. Researchers have sequenced the genomes of an old and young Aldabra giant tortoise to compare with other long-lived species and with less long-lived giant tortoises, part of a continuing effort to better understand aging via comparative biology. There is that hope that the comparative biology of aging can identify which mechanisms of aging are most important, as well as identify specific biochemical differences in long-lived species that may one day form the basis for therapies to slow aging in humans.
